title: Capacity healing checklist and rollback heuristics for cross-tenant interference
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: After a recent dedicated cluster capacity event, we observed severe cross-tenant interference where one workload caused sustained slowdowns and elevated evictions for nearby reservations. This ticket captures an executable checklist for immediate healing (short-term), plus deterministic rollback heuristics for any rapid policy changes applied to reservations or burst controls.
investigation_summary: Telemetry shows a single tenant with a previously unseen sequence-length distribution that created prolonged KV-cache churn and oversized prefetch behavior, causing kernel-level queuing and deprioritization of other reservations. Autoscaling reacted by expanding ephemeral burst capacity which amplified noisy neighbor effects. Reservation accounting showed skew: several tenants reported sustained utilization above their reservation for 25+ minutes leading to eviction cascades.
root_causes: Uncapped burst tokens allowed extended overutilization beyond intended short windows
Reservation sizing was based on 95th percentile traffic but did not account for correlated long-sequence spikes
KV-cache reclamation policy favored aggressive eviction without tenant-aware heuristics
Lack of an automated circuit-breaker to throttle a single tenant when eviction rates cross a threshold
short_term_mitigations: Apply emergency soft-throttle to the offending tenant (Marco Chen) — reduced burst window from 60s to 10s
Temporarily disable global autoscale-burst for the affected cluster and revert to conservative static burst pool
Increase reservation enforcement delta: reduce soft-overcommit cap from 1.5x to 1.1x for 2 hours
Enable 'eviction-protect' flag for reservations with recent SLA violations to prevent cascading evictions
long_term_fixes: Implement tenant-level burst budget metering and sliding-window burn rate alarms (owner: Riley Patel)
Revise reservation sizing tool to incorporate sequence-length and KV-cache pressure heuristics (owner: Sofia Martinez)
Introduce tenant-aware KV-cache reclamation that preserves hot prefixes tied to pinned reservations
Add a cluster circuit-breaker that runs eviction-rate SLO checks and triggers progressive throttles and alerting
Design automated reservation resizer that suggests ops-approved adjustments with canary rollout

Customer comms draft for impacted customers with remediation timeline (owner: Priya Shah, Customer Ops, due: 2026-03-06)
acceptance_criteria: Cluster no longer shows eviction spikes >2x baseline in 72 hour synthetic validation window
Burst policy changes have a safe default and respect max-burst-duration; unit tests + PR merged
Reservation-sizing tool provides suggested delta and a canary rollout plan; PM sign-off achieved
Grafana panels emit alerts for eviction-rate > 0.8% sustained for 3m and on-call runbook referenced
rollback_plan: Any changes to burst controls or reservation enforcement will be rolled back via a single automation job. Rollback triggers: increase in evictions >1.5x baseline within 30m after change, error-rate regressions for customer API >0.5%, or unexplained latency tail growth. Team will notify on-call and open a SEV channel; rollback job will revert cluster-level flags and redeploy previous policy within 10 minutes.
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for max-burst-duration enforcement. 2) Integration test: two synthetic tenants (one steady, one bursty) run for 6h to validate eviction containment. 3) Chaos-run: induce KV-cache pressure and validate tenant-aware reclamation does not evict hot prefixes. 4) Post-merge canary: enable new policy in single cluster for 24h with monitoring and automatic rollback hooks.

Aim to avoid manual cluster-wide tweaks; prefer targeted tenant mitigations and automated rollback triggers. Follow-up ticket will track migration of burst budgeting into billing surfaces so customers see burn rates.
